evidence.snippet: block the SGLT2 protein within the kidneys, inhibiting glucose reabsorption, and causing an associated osmotic diuresis
evidence.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors (-flozin drugs, including empagliflozin) block the SGLT2 protein in the kidneys.

paper.title: Cardiovascular benefits from SGLT2 inhibition in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients is not impaired with phosphate flux related to pharmacotherapy.

evidence.snippet: the compensatory effect of SGLT1 in renal glucose reabsorption (RGR) when SGLT2 is inhibited
evidence.explanation: SGLT2 mediates renal glucose reabsorption; inhibiting SGLT2 reduces this process.

paper.title: Mechanistic Modeling of Empagliflozin: Predicting Pharmacokinetics, Urinary Glucose Excretion, and Investigating Compensatory Role of SGLT1 in Renal Glucose Reabsorption.

evidence.snippet: empagliflozin lowers blood glucose via reduced tubular reabsorption of filtered glucose
evidence.explanation: Reduced tubular reabsorption of filtered glucose causes filtered glucose to be excreted in the urine (glycosuria) instead of reabsorbed.

paper.title: Regression of diabetic nephropathy by treatment with empagliflozin in BTBR ob/ob mice.
paper.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association

paper.title: Empagliflozin and Renal Sodium-Hydrogen Exchange in Healthy Subjects.
paper.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

evidence.snippet: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by elevated blood glucose levels due to insulin deficiency or resistance
evidence.explanation: Elevated blood glucose is the defining feature of type 2 diabetes mellitus; empagliflozin exerts its therapeutic effect by lowering blood glucose.
